historical_timeline.summary: First recording; national fame from 1956; Army service from 1958 to 1960; Las Vegas engagements and tours in the 1970s. Believed never to have smoked or drunk alcohol.
Acute angle-closure glaucoma; under an ophthalmologist's care from then on.
Hospital stay in Memphis under an assumed name; later testimony says he was withdrawn from narcotic drugs.
A few weeks off at Graceland after a year of engagements and tours.
Las Vegas engagement, then a tour from September 27 to October 14.
Two hospital stays in 1975, for abdominal problems and swelling and then for breathlessness and swelling; reported treatment for hypertension and a blocked, enlarged colon.
About 19,000 doses of stimulants, sedatives and painkillers prescribed by one physician in his last 30 months, with drugs also from other sources.
Dies at Graceland at 42; the cause is disputed. Overweight in his last years; his glaucoma is later interpreted as steroid-induced.
His physician is acquitted of overprescribing after testimony that he was addicted to prescribed drugs.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: Polypharmacy and prescription opioid and sedative use disorders from several prescribers, in a 39-year-old touring singer who comes in for fatigue, weight gain, constipation, sleepiness and high blood pressure. The episode covers a brown-bag medication reconciliation and prescription drug monitoring program review that finds two opioids, two benzodiazepines and an appetite suppressant from five prescribers; a nonjudgmental DSM-5-TR assessment; naloxone at the first visit; a single-prescriber agreement; buprenorphine started in the office under the ASAM 1968 guideline, with the guideline's advice that taking a benzodiazepine is not a reason to withhold it; the benzodiazepines combined into diazepam and tapered slowly under the 1973 joint guideline; a structured safety assessment with means safety and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; hypertension confirmed with home readings and treated under the 1973 AHA/ACC guideline; obesity treated without stigma with tirzepatide, which also treats obstructive sleep apnea; STOP-Bang and in-laboratory polysomnography because opioids make home testing unreliable; opioid-induced constipation; glaucoma that rules out phentermine and anticholinergic sleep aids; acute back pain managed on buprenorphine; and care planned around a performing and touring schedule.

visit_schedule.purpose: Establishing primary care for fatigue, weight gain, constipation, daytime sleepiness and high blood pressure, with many prescribed drugs from several prescribers: a full medication reconciliation and prescription drug monitoring program review, a nonjudgmental substance use assessment, safety, and an addiction medicine referral

Three-week review on buprenorphine: withdrawal and cravings, the first benzodiazepine taper step, blood pressure treatment, CPAP, constipation and weight, and planning for a Las Vegas engagement
Same-day sick visit for low back pain
Ten-week review after the Las Vegas engagement and a back strain: buprenorphine, the taper, weight treatment, sleep apnea and planning for a three-week tour
Four-month review after the tour: recovery, the taper, blood pressure, weight, liver tests, sleep and the plan ahead
